item.title: Gold Tweezers?
item.content:encoded:
I could understand if these are gold-plated tweezers, but if they are pure gold, which the article seems to imply, then the tweezers would be useless. They would be bent out of shape by the wielder's hand during the hair picking phase. You'd need to kill a lot of people to reacquire the amount of gold needed to fix any damage to 221.

I understand the compulsion sets in after one use, so the tweezers aren't necessary for ripping out more difficult materials, but still. I don't know why I'm being so pedantic about this.

item.title: The truly horrible thing about this...
item.content:encoded:
…is that diagnostically, to have OCD, the person who has the compulsion must be aware that the compulsion is irrational and serves no purpose.

The people who are ripping parts out of themselves here, according to this, are not delusional: they know perfectly well this is pointless.

(If they think it has a purpose, that's a different thing (OCPD)).

item.title: Tweaks and holes
item.content:encoded:
When listing the process of removing things, external organs should probably be listed before internal organs, since removing the latter tends to be fatal much more quickly.

Also, for the test subject, you should probably name the internal organs - perhaps he died holding loops of his own bowel, pulled out through a hole he gouged in his abdomen?

What happens if the subject is restrained after removing SCP-221 from the subject?
